To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Dynamic Recurrent Layer is an efficient, interpretable and flexible neural network layer that can be trained on a wide range of data and can be used to model complex systems in a data driven manner.

1) The new Dynamic Recurrent Network (DRN) layer is a new layer type for neural networks, 2) The DRN layer is based on the equations of basic linear systems and can thus be interpreted as an interpretable layer, 3) The DRN is a general layer type and can be used together with other neural network layer types and can be used for sequence-to-sequence learning, and 4) The DRN can be used for system identification and provides results

we propose a novel recurrent layer type, the Dynamic Recurrrent Network, for data driven modelling of complex physical systems, which is based on the difference equations of basic system transfer functions and can be trained using gradient descent, and that this layer type yields results on several system identification benchmark problems comparable or better than other state of the ar neural layer types.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions:

* A new recurrent network layer, the Dynamic Recurring Network (DRN), based on discrete difference equations, which can be used in conjunction with other network layers for data driven modelling and system identification.
a novel recurrent neural network architecture, the DRN, based on the theory of dynamic systems.
the following research questions:  1) How can we use deep learning to model the dynamics of complex physical systems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed DRN layer is an interesting alternative for recurrent layers in neural networks, which can be used for system identification and time series prediction, and can provide more insights about the underlying system.
the DRN is a very promising approach for data-driven modelling of complex dynamic systems.
the Dynamic Recurrent Layer is a very promising new layer type for system identification and modelling of dynamic physical systems, which has to be investigated further in future studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel network layer type that is based on the theory of dynamic systems, which can be used to model time series data in an explainable way and yields comparable or better results than existing state of the art recurrent network layers.
we propose a new type of recurrent layer, which allows to use dynamic systems theory for data driven modelling of complex physical systems.
we propose a new layer type, which is more explainable, more robust and can be trained with gradient descent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of network layer type can be a key factor to improve the performance of a deep neural network in complex system identification tasks.
the proposed Dynamic Recurrent Network can be used to build explainable models for complex physical systems and can provide insight into the system's time dependent behaviour.

the choice of the computation function is an important design parameter for neural network layers and that the use of a computation function based on discrete difference equations can provide additional benefits for the model interpretability and robustness.
